lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Check that the profile URL is the live, intended link.
items.because: A working link lets a reviewer verify your background.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality for typical U.S. applications.
items.because: They usually do not help assess qualifications and may introduce irrelevant personal information.

items.says: Put Brightcart before Pinecrest.
items.because: Reverse chronological order makes the most recent experience easiest to find.

items.says: Do not present daily p-value checks and stopping below 0.05 as sound test practice.
items.because: That stopping rule can inflate false-positive risk.

items.says: Say what decision or analysis you actually owned.
Avoid implying the shift move alone caused the drop in hold times if other changes affected them.
items.because: The shift move may not have been the only change affecting hold times.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
Be ready to substantiate how the reduction in review errors was measured.
Separate the fraud-extract automation from the other duties, or cut the less relevant duties.
Clarify which work saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
items.because: The current list of duties makes the source of the saving unclear.

items.says: Qualify the claim that the dashboard lifted repeat purchases unless you can show causation.
items.because: The increase from 22% to 27% does not itself show that the dashboard or retargeting caused it.

items.says: Correct the join logic for finding customers with no orders.
items.because: A left join from orders to customers followed by a null customer name may identify unmatched records or missing names instead.

items.says: Fix the attribution-model sentence’s grammar.
items.because: Its opening action phrase does not connect cleanly to “raised.”

items.says: Clarify what “dbt-style” means if you did not use dbt.
Specify your contribution to the funded recommendations if they were shared work.
Ensure the halving of ad hoc requests uses comparable before-and-after periods.
Define the percentage-based error metric or denominator behind “12% mean absolute error.”
items.because: Mean absolute error ordinarily has the units of the quantity predicted.

items.says: Correct the claimed 50% reduction in empty-station hours.
items.because: A drop from 300 to 200 is a 33% reduction.

items.says: Make clear the empty-station result was a replay or simulation.
items.because: It was not a real-world operational result.

items.says: Correct the claim that the hit rate rose by 15%.
items.because: A rise from 60% to 75% is 15 percentage points, or a 25% relative increase.

items.says: Define “hit rate.”
items.because: Readers need to know what counted as a hit.

items.says: Avoid attributing the entire wait-time reduction solely to the shift move if other changes affected it.
Verify that “9,000 handwritten visit logs” accurately describes the records.
Verify that the household-matching method supports the unique-household count.
Consider adding tools used confidently in the roles or projects.
items.because: The experience mentions dashboards and SQL modeling without naming their platforms.

items.says: Make sure “forecasting” and “metric design” reflect work you personally did and can explain.
